item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 011114
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 AM PDT Tue Sep 1 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Karina, located well west-southwest of the southern tip of the Baja
California Peninsula, on Tropical Storm Lowell, located several
hundred miles southeast of the Hawaiian Islands, and on newly formed
Tropical Storm Marie, located several hundred miles southwest of
southwestern Mexico.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected during the next 7 days.

&&
Public advisories on Tropical Storm Marie are issued under WMO
header WTPZ33 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPEP3.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Storm Marie are issued under WMO
header WTPZ23 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCMEP3.

$$

WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 AM HST (1500 UTC), the center of Hurricane Karina was located 
near latitude 18.1 North, longitude 129.0 West. Karina is moving 
toward the west near 12 mph (19 km/h), and a westward to 
west-northwestward motion is expected during the next few days. 
 
Maximum sustained winds remain near 140 mph (220 km/h) with higher
gusts.  Karina is a category 4 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson
Hurricane Wind Scale.  Gradual weakening is expected during the 
next several days.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 35 miles (55 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 115 miles
(185 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 945 mb (27.91 inches).

item.title: Hurricane Karina Forecast Discussion Number 21
item.description:
Issued at 500 AM HST Tue Sep 01 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 011431
TCDEP1
 
Hurricane Karina Discussion Number  21
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP112026
500 AM HST Tue Sep 01 2026
 
Karina remains a powerful category 4 hurricane, although there are 
some signs that the cyclone might be near its peak intensity. Over 
the past few hours, the eye has become cloud-filled and the 
convective pattern is not quite as symmetric. A blend of the latest 
satellite intensity estimates supports maintaining the initial 
intensity at 120 kt.  Despite being very strong, the overall cloud 
pattern and wind field are relatively compact. 

The major hurricane is moving westward at about 10 kt. A general 
slow westward to west-northwestward motion is expected during the 
next 3 to 4 days as a narrow mid-level ridge remains situated to the 
north of the hurricane. Over the weekend, a turn to the northwest 
seems likely as the ridge shifts eastward and as the cyclone 
approaches a mid- to upper-level low north of Hawaii. Little change 
was made to the previous track forecast, except for a nudge to the 
north toward the end of the period. This track forecast is based on 
a blend of the HCCA, GDMI, and TVCN models. It should be noted that 
there is a fair amount of spread from days 3 to 5, and confidence in 
that part of the track forecast is lower than average.

Karina is forecast to gradually lose strength over the next several 
days. Although the wind shear is expected to remain low for the 
next few days, progressively cooler SSTs and decreasing relative 
humidity values should cause steady weakening. However, the 
hurricane could become annular, which might cause it to weaken at a 
slower pace than average. The models are unanimous in showing 
weakening, but vary on the rate. The NHC intensity forecast is 
similar to the previous one, and lies a little above the model 
consensus.

----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...15.0N 108.7W
ABOUT 400 MI...645 KM SW OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...45 MPH...75 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 315 DEGREES AT 9 MPH...15 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1002 MB...29.59 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 AM MST (1500 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Marie was
located near latitude 15.0 North, longitude 108.7 West. Marie is
moving toward the northwest near 9 mph (15 km/h), and a turn toward 
the west-northwest is expected on Thursday.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 45 mph (75 km/h) with higher gusts.
Gradual strengthening is forecast, and Marie is expected to become
a hurricane by Wednesday night.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 205 miles (335 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1002 mb (29.59 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Marie will affect portions of the coast
of southwest Mexico and the Baja California Peninsula for the next
few days and will likely spread northward to southern California 
over the weekend.  These swells are likely to cause 
life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please consult
products from your local weather office. A depiction of rip current
risk for the United States can be found at:
hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep1.shtml?ripCurrents
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 PM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Roberts

item.title: Tropical Storm Marie Forecast Discussion Number 2
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM MST Tue Sep 01 2026 
000
WTPZ43 KNHC 011441
TCDEP3
 
Tropical Storm Marie Discussion Number   2
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP132026
800 AM MST Tue Sep 01 2026
 
This morning's GOES-18 Proxy-VIS satellite imagery indicates that
Marie is gradually becoming better organized.  Deep convection with 
cold cloud tops of -81C is developing over the surface circulation 
center, and a spiral band is wrapping around the center from the 
southwest part of the cyclone.  No changes yet in both the 
subjective and objective satellite intensity guidance, however, so 
the initial intensity is held at 40 kt for this advisory.
 
The ocean is warm, the low- to mid-levels of the atmosphere are
moist, and the deep-layer shear is low.  Subsequently, strengthening
is expected, and Marie should become a hurricane by Wednesday 
night.  By the weekend, the GFS/ECMWF SHIPS statistical intensity 
guidance and the physics-based deterministic models indicate that 
Marie will encounter a drier, stable marine layer air mass while 
traversing progressively cooler oceanic temperatures.  Accordingly, 
the NHC intensity forecast follows suit and shows Marie slowly 
weakening beyond day 4.
 
An earlier 0707 UTC OSCAT-3 scatterometer overpass and a
fortuitous 1247 UTC GPM/GMI image indicated that the surface center 
was a bit farther northeast than previously noted, and near 
the northwestern edge of the deep convective canopy.  Marie's 
initial motion is estimated to be northwestward, or 315/8 kt.  A 
mid-tropospheric subtropical ridge stretching from northern
Mexico westward over the extreme eastern Pacific should steer
the cyclone generally northwestward through Thursday.  
Afterward, the subtropical high should weaken in response to an 
amplifying mid- to upper-level trough approaching the west coast of 
the U.S. This change in the large-scale synoptic pattern is 
expected to slow Marie's forward speed.  For the remainder of the 
forecast, the aforementioned mid- to upper-level trough should fill 
and lift northeastward, allowing the ridge to build and reestablish 
north of Marie and steer the system back toward the west-northwest 
through the weekend.  There's still quite a bit of cross-track 
spread in the model suite beyond day 3, with one cluster indicating 
a north-northwestward motion while another model cluster shows a 
more west-northwestward trajectory.  The official forecast reflects 
slight adjustments to the left of the previous forecast and favors 
a blend of the skilled NOAA HCCA consensus aid and the Google 
DeepMind FNv3 ensemble mean forecast.
